stem: A practitioner wants to issue multiple separate Schedule II prescriptions for the same patient on one visit. Which federal conditions are consistent with the multiple-prescription pathway? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The practitioner should postdate each later prescription with its future fill date
The set automatically becomes refillable because it covers more than one month
The prescriptions together may authorize up to a 90-day total supply
The later prescriptions may include written instructions identifying the earliest date on which they may be filled
The prescriptions must be issued for a legitimate medical purpose in the usual course of professional practice

explanation.core_reasoning: Multiple separate C-II prescriptions can cover up to 90 days when federal conditions are met; later fills use earliest-fill instructions rather than postdating.

choice_analysis.A: The prescriptions are issued on the actual date; earliest-fill instructions are used instead.
choice_analysis.B: Separate C-II prescriptions are not refills.
choice_analysis.C: Federal law permits a total not exceeding 90 days when conditions are met.
choice_analysis.D: Earliest-fill instructions are part of the pathway.

related_facts: The regulation does not create a federal entitlement to receive 90 days in every case.
explanation.mpje_trap: Calling sequential prescriptions refills or postdating them.

reasoning_steps: Recognize separate C-II prescriptions rather than refills
Apply total-supply, fill-date, and legitimate-purpose conditions
